look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: follow the low, hairy, branching annual stems to individual terminal daisy heads. Check alternate narrow-to-spatulate leaves and the overlapping, pale-margined phyllaries under a head. For the hard separation from perennial A. riddellii, inspect plant duration/root and mature cypsela hairs with magnification; white rays alone are not diagnostic.

project_inclusion.notes: Accepted taxon native to Texas at state level. No three-target-county PASS assigned; source-pool learner admission is independent of range certification.

taxonomy_notes: Accepted species under POWO and Flora of North America. The species includes varieties kidderi, skirrhobasis, and thalassius; source row does not establish an infraspecific identity. Do not silently install a variety-level duplicate.

morphology_keys.habit: Taprooted annual, low and branching; stems often decumbent to ascending, hairy, commonly forming loose mounds.
morphology_keys.leaves_attachment: Basal and alternate stem leaves, sessile or short-petiolate, from oblanceolate to narrow-lanceolate; lower leaves may be toothed or lobed while upper leaves can be less divided. Surface hairs are visible at close range.
morphology_keys.flower_reproductive: One radiate flower head at the end of a stalk; white rays (sometimes pinkish beneath) surround yellow disc florets. Under each head are several overlapping rows of phyllaries with pale, scarious margins; receptacle conical and without chaff.
morphology_keys.fruit_seed: Mature dry one-seeded cypselae are angular/strongly ribbed, often with short duplex hairs curved at the tip; the pappus is a short crown or small scales. Mature disc-corolla bases can become bulbously swollen. Fruit hair form and corolla-base details require a microscope or macro.
morphology_keys.stem_bud: Check soft to spreading hairs on branches and the solitary nodding-to-upright head buds; do not use bud posture alone as species proof.

confused_with: Aphanostephus pilosus (annual; straighter cypsela hairs and generally fewer rays)
comparisons.key_distinctions: A. skirrhobasis is annual and develops bulbously swollen mature disc-corolla bases and one-directionally coiled cypsela hairs; A. riddellii is perennial, has unswollen mature disc-corolla bases and glochidiate/pronged cypsela hairs. These decisive fruit traits need magnification. Erigeron generally differs in the combination of phyllaries, conical receptacle, fruit ribs and pappus; never separate by flower color alone.
